events.text: In BIAN v14.0, the Product Directory Service Domain maintains and exposes the catalog of financial products offered by the institution. It is the authoritative source of product definitions and configuration templates, referenced by other Service Domains when products are instantiated or used.
The Product Directory manages: Product Identity, Product Classification, Operational / Sales & Marketing / Servicing & Production Requirements, and Product Features & Specifications.
Classification: This is a Product Definition Domain — not a runtime domain, not a customer-specific domain. Data is product-level, configuration-driven, variant-specific, and institution-defined.

rows: Product Directory SD Does NOT Manage
Customer agreements — Sales Product Agreement SD
Operational account state — Savings/Current Account SDs
Live account balances or transaction states

events.text: Products in Thought Machine are structured in a three-tier hierarchy exposed through the Product Directory:

rows: Top-level product group (e.g. current_account). Retrieved via GET /v1/products. One CR per product family.
Base product definition within a family. Contains the foundational parameter set. Identified by tags[0] = LEVEL_TEMPLATE.
Specific product offering derived from a template. Identified by tags[0] = LEVEL_VARIANT and PARENT_VERSION tag linking back to template.

events.text: A ProductReference field is used inside the CR payload. ProductReference is an array of Product objects where each element represents one product version (template or variant) of the same core product family.
ProductIdentification is also structured as an array within each ProductReference element, allowing multiple identification types per product version:

rows: Product family / smart contract ID assigned by the bank
Smart contract version ID — uniquely identifies the template or variant
Parent version linkage — present only on variant entries, derived from PARENT_VERSION tag (numeric ID only)
Map to ProductIdentification with ProductIdentificationType = Stylenumber; extract numeric ID only (e.g. 101, not PARENT_VERSION=101)
3 entries in ProductIdentification[]: Suppliersitemnumber + Modelnumber + Stylenumber
Via Suppliersitemnumber — identifies the product family
DirectoryEntryDateType, DirectoryEntryDate, DirectoryEntryStatus sit outside the ProductReference[] array

events.text: ProductVersion carries the display version from TM (e.g. 1.0.0, 1.1.0) — distinct from the smart contract version ID stored in Modelnumber.
A new custom endpoint compliant with BIAN Behavior Qualifier type is introduced to support product catalog page load:

items: Endpoint: GET /ProductDirectory/Product/Retrieve
Purpose: Lists all products available in TM. Internally mapped to GET /v1/products.
Filter applied internally: is_internal = false — excludes test and internal products.
Response: ProductListing[] array — high-level product records only, used to render product family cards.

events.text: The Sales and Marketing BQ captures marketing-related definitions, features, pricing, and eligibility information for a specific product version (template or variant).

items: salesandmarketingid = TM smart contract version ID (same value as Modelnumber in ProductReference[]).
The BQ payload is an array of elements — not a single object.
Endpoint: GET /ProductDirectory/{productdirectoryid}/SalesandMarketing/{salesandmarketingid}/Retrieve

rows: Full parameter set from TM — one entry per parameter. Includes feature type, ID, name, specification, and effective date.
Pricing-related parameters from TM, classified by ProductFeatureModalityType
Fee and penalty parameters from TM, classified by ProductFeatureModalityType
Suitability classification for the product variant
Default type: SalesAndMarketingRequirement. Specification derived from is_optional: OPTIONAL / NOT OPTIONAL

events.text: The adapter applies different transformation logic depending on whether the version is a template or variant:

items: LEVEL_VARIANT: maps directly to product_versions.params.value.
LEVEL_TEMPLATE (conditional):

events.text: ◦ If params[i].number exists → format as range(min: X, max: Y, step: Z)
◦ If params[i].values exists → format as values(option1, option2, ...)
◦ If params[i].account exists with key-value pairs → flatten to key: value, ...; if empty → leave blank
The Product Directory supports a structured navigation flow from product families through templates to variants:

Step 5.3 Efficiency: Zero additional API calls are made when listing variants. The ProductReference[] array retrieved in step 5.2 is held in client state and filtered entirely on the front end — variant navigation is instantaneous with no server load.
Both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously:

items: ProductPriority === LEVEL_VARIANT
ProductIdentification[] contains an entry where ProductIdentificationType === Stylenumber AND IdentifierValue === Modelnumber of the selected template

Authoritative source for product version data, parameters, and tags. Product Directory adapter wraps TM product-versions API.

events.text: When calling the product-versions API, the adapter must always pass the page token together with the product_id. Paginating with only the product_id returns only the first page. Both parameters must be included in every paginated request to ensure all product variants are retrieved.

In the Dev environment, the products API may return test or internal products. The adapter must apply filtering to exclude such products before returning results to the Product Management application, based on agreed metadata or identification rules.

For products and their variants to be visible through the TM adapter, corresponding smart contracts must be created and uploaded in Thought Machine. Products that have not been uploaded will not appear in Product Directory results.
